Dear Phil,

I tried to convey a DIF analysis for an 8-item scale containing the dichotomous items

 "Q1"  "Q7"  "Q10" "Q11" "Q12" "Q30" "Q32" "Q33"

 For that purpose I estimated a multipleGroup-model

 

mymodel = multipleGroup(mydata, 1, group=mygroup, itemtype="2PL", SE=TRUE,

invariance=c("Q10","Q30","free_mean","free_var"))   # Q10 and Q30 used as anchors

 

followed by the DIF, excluding the anchor items:

 

DIF(mymodel,which.par=c("a1","d"),items2test=c("Q1","Q7","Q11","Q12","Q32","Q33"))

 

now I obtain the following output:

 

   |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++| 100% elapsed=11s

     converged     AIC   SABIC      HQ     BIC     X2 df     p

Q1       TRUE   2.106  10.183   6.990  16.539  1.894  2 0.388

Q7       TRUE -30.737 -22.660 -25.853 -16.304 34.737 2     0

Q10      TRUE   0.000   0.000   0.000   0.000      0  0 NaN   ???

Q11      TRUE -19.990 -11.913 -15.106  -5.557  23.99 2     0

Q12      TRUE  -8.903  -0.826  -4.019   5.530 12.903  2 0.002

Q30      TRUE   0.000   0.000   0.000   0.000      0  0 NaN   ???

 

I am surprised by the output: Why are Q10 and Q30 (the anchor items) listed, but Q32 and Q33 (the last 2 items) missing? Is it just mislabeled or were the wrong items tested (I assume the latter, as X2=0, but who knows?).


Thank you very much for your support!

Milica

parts:
Hi Milica,

The default constraint method in DIF() is the 'add' scheme, which adds equality constraints to create the nested model structure for testing. In this case items Q10 and Q30 already had their parameters and subsequent estimates constrained to be equal as they are anchors, so there's no additional constraint additions to be made. You could, however, test whether the anchors themselves contain DIF using the 'drop' approach, though you do run the risk of losing empirical identification if the model isn't sufficiently constrained to do so (2 items for anchoring is close to the bare minimum....). HTH.

Phil
